column4: which source the tunnel comes from. "channelsdb" = the entry is
annotated and its tunnels are fetched; "caver" = nothing in the PDB
that matches this enzyme is annotated, so CAVER is run on the entry.
a HOMOLOGOUS deposited structure, not the iMARS construct itself:
the paper's enzymes are plant and yeast proteins and almost none has
its own crystal structure. Found by RCSB sequence search on the
parent sequence, then filtered by whether ChannelsDB has it.
RCSB sequence-search score against the iMARS parent sequence,
1.0000 = top hit. Below ~0.6 the entry is a DISTANT homolog and its
tunnel is evidence about the family, not about this enzyme.
where that entry sat in the search. ChannelsDB coverage is per
ENTRY, not per protein: only 4 of the 24 rank-1 hits are annotated,
and going down the ranks found 22. The rank is kept because a rank-12
hit is a weaker claim than a rank-1 hit even at the same score.
what this enzyme HANDS ON, when it is the upstream half of a pair:
the channelled intermediate. Blank for an enzyme that only ever
appears downstream in this set, because then nothing here consumes
its product.
which chain of that entry to prepare. On the ChannelsDB branch
this FOLLOWS THE TUNNEL: a report annotates tunnels of the whole
deposited assembly, and four of these entries annotate a protomer
other than chain A (ADS/BBS chain B, GPPS chain D, LIC chain B).
Prepping chain A there leaves the tunnel floating 20-32 A from
the protein -- geometry about a protomer no longer in the file.
run_examples.py re-checks this at run time and refuses a tunnel
that is not attached to the chain it prepared.
